look_here_first: Texas groundplum variety with thick green fleshy pods near the ground. The important look-alike is A. plattensis: compare ovary/pod HAIRS (groundplum generally glabrous versus hairy plattensis) and groove along each pod SUTURE, not just the pod's size.

lookalikes.differences: Not the only thick-podded genus member: A. plattensis also has green fleshy groundplum-like fruit and can be sympatric in south-central Texas. An ovary hair macro, 1 mm scale and mature suture-groove photo are necessary. Var. berlandieri is a distinct accepted taxon: photos of var. crassicarpus must not be labeled as this Texas variety.
